subject: GPU matrix + activation wave plan for Aurorix procurement
messages:
From: Ro han Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@aurorix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU matrix + activation wave plan for Aurorix procurement

Priya — thanks for the time yesterday. Attaching a concise proposal for how Redwood would structure a dedicated cluster for Aurorix, with two activation waves so you can ramp without a single large upfront commitment. High level: 

- Baseline: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs (min-guarantee) for predictable throughput during pilot and compliance testing.
- Wave 1 (30 days): Warm pool of 24 + 8 burstable GPUs; expected steady-state throughput for dev and small-scale production.
- Wave 2 (90 days post-signing): Scale to 72 GPUs to support full production models and peak inference windows.

Key notes:
- We recommend a 24-GPU minimum so KV cache + prefix caching gives you consistent latency at production sequence lengths.
- Autoscaling policy: maintain min=24, scale steps of +8 GPUs with 15-minute cool-down.
- Quantization profile: int8 for generative routes, float16 for high-accuracy reranking (we include tradeoffs).

I attached a short MPU profile (aurorix_mpu_profile_v1.xlsx) showing token-per-second estimates by model family and a PDF with the three capacity options and burn-rate projections. Please let me know the procurement timeline and any PO/contract constraints. I copied Ben on capacity/pricing specifics. 

Next steps: can you confirm target go-live quarter and whether Aurorix needs a hard minimum GPU cap in the contract (some procurement teams do)? If you want, we can convert this into a draft SOW for legal review.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta

Rohan — thanks for the proposal. A few clarifying questions from procurement and engineering: 

1) Can you confirm the contractual minimum GPU count and whether we can drop below 24 during low usage (e.g., weekends) while preserving the KV cache? Procurement prefers flexibility but engineering wants cache persistence.
2) What are the SLA implications if we burst beyond Wave 2 (72 GPUs)? Any price step-ups or preemption risk?
3) We need an explicit ramp schedule tied to milestone payments — procurement needs dates and acceptance criteria.

Procurement note: Aurorix prefers quarterly billing and requires a 45-day notice for de-scope. Also — do you support invoice-level line items per GPU tranche?

Would appreciate a compact table with effective dates, min GPUs, max burst, and pricing bands. Can you loop in account lead for commercial terms?

Best,
Priya Shah

pri ya@aurorix.ai
From: Ro han Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GPU matrix + activation wave plan for Aurorix procurement

Priya — thanks, great questions. Short answers first, then a compact table below.

1) Contractual minimum: we can set a hard contractual minimum of 24 GPUs for the Dedicated cluster. Operationally we support a warm-sleep mode that allows reducing active capacity for cost savings while keeping a persistent KV store — the win is preserved latency; fee structure: 60% of the min-GPU monthly charge applies in warm-sleep so you don't pay full active rate.

2) Bursting beyond Wave 2: we guarantee capacity for the committed maximum (72 GPUs) in the contract. For bursts above that, we offer transient spot bursts up to +20 GPUs subject to availability; pricing is higher (spot uplift) and not SLA-backed. No preemption on committed GPUs; spot bursts are best-effort.

3) Ramp schedule + milestones: we can align waves to milestones and payments. Proposed acceptance criteria:
- Milestone A (Day 0 signing): infra provisioning complete, cluster baseline ready (24 GPUs configured), integration checklist items 1–5 passed. Payment: 30% of committed monthly base for first month.
- Milestone B (Day 30): Wave 1 activation complete (32 GPUs active); performance tests pass under 99th pct latency goal. Payment: 30% of first quarter pro-rated.
- Milestone C (Day 90): Full production activation (72 GPUs); runbook and handoff complete. Payment: remaining 40% of initial quarter and adjust monthly billing to full committed level.

Compact table (effective dates are illustrative):
- 2028-09-01 to 2028-09-30 | min=24 | burstable up to 32 | billing: warm-sleep 60% of min-rate | acceptance: infra smoke tests
- 2028-10-01 to 2029-01-31 | min=32 | burstable up to 48 | billing: full-rate for active GPUs, spot for overage | acceptance: perf + load 95% window
- 2029-02-01 onwards | min=72 | burstable up to 92 | billing: committed monthly rate per GPU tranche | acceptance: production SLA sign-off

I attached the same spreadsheets; Ben and Marissa — any constraints on discounting for a multi-quarter ramp? Marissa, can you confirm commercial lead and whether we should include onboarding credits for the first 60 days?

Cheers,
Rohan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in quickly — good structure. Two commercial items to confirm before we send a formal SOW:

- Discount: suggest we offer a 12% volume discount if Aurorix signs to min=72 within 120 days of pilot completion (this incentivizes faster ramp). If procurement insists on quarterly billing only, propose a billing credit for onboarding equal to 10% of first-quarter charges.
- Notice window: procurement asked for 45-day de-scope notice. We can accept with a step-down charge equal to 50% of the difference between committed min and new min for the remainder of that billing period.

Ben — please prepare a pricing band table reflecting 24/32/72 tranches with the 12% conditional discount and the warm-sleep 60% fallback. I'll draft SOW language around milestone payments and acceptance criteria.
